> 13.5.1 Verify that debug modes are disabled in production environments for every component to prevent exposure of debug features and unintended information leakage.

A bit hard to read.

---

> 13.5.2 Verify that directory browsing is disabled unless deliberately desired.

Proposal:
> 13.5.2 Verify that directory browsing is disabled in the web server configuration unless deliberately desired.

---

> 13.5.3 Verify that the HTTP TRACE method is disabled to avoid potential information leakage.

Proposal:
> 13.5.3 Verify that usage of the HTTP TRACE method is not allowed to avoid potential information leakage.

---

> 13.5.5 Verify that the web tier is configured to serve only files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information and source code leakage. For example, backup files (.bak), temporary working files (.swp), compressed files (.zip, .tar.gz), and other extensions commonly used by editors must be blocked unless required.

I think the reasoning in this requirement is so year 2000. Probably I have voted to keep this requirement in the past, but maybe we should just delete it..

Not sure how I did not notice it during PR, but this for sure quite ironic update [proposal](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2954#issuecomment-2802882773) from Jim:
> 13.5.2 Verify that web servers do not expose directory listings to clients unless explicitly intended and documented.

For this requirement, I don't think the "and documented" is necessary.

So the proposal is:
> 13.5.2 Verify that web servers do not expose directory listings to clients unless explicitly intended.

Not sure how I did not notice it during PR, but this for sure quite ironic update [proposal](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2954#issuecomment-2802882773) from Jim:
> 13.5.2 Verify that web servers do not expose directory listings to clients unless explicitly intended and documented.

For this requirement, I don't think the "and documented" is necessary.
